about.title: Albany Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Albany is a small city, but its traffic doesn't feel small during Friday rush hour, when reported crashes tend to cluster between 3 and 5 p.m. along corridors like I-80, San Pablo Avenue, Solano Avenue, and Marin Avenue. In a recent year, Alameda County recorded 66 injury collisions in Albany, with 89 people hurt and one traffic death — numbers that represent real neighbors, commuters, and families. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the period right after matters: insurance adjusters move fast, evidence disappears, and stress can make it hard to know what to do next. We handle personal injury claims and don't charge you anything upfront. Our team works on contingency, so you only pay if you recover compensation. We can help you focus on healing while we handle the insurance calls and paperwork.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls Again

items.title: California's Fault Rules Can Work in Your Favor
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly responsible for the crash. We can help make sure your share of fault isn't inflated by the insurance company.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit, but claims against a government entity — like the City of Albany or Caltrans for a road defect — can require notice in as little as six months. Missing that window can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: What You Say Can Be Used Against You
items.desc: Giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer isn't required, and it can create problems later even when you're just trying to be honest. We can speak for you and help protect evidence from the crash scene before it's lost.

items.question: Do I have to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: No, you're not obligated to provide one, and it's often better not to until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use recorded statements to find reasons to reduce or deny a claim. We can communicate with the insurer on your behalf.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in Albany?
items.answer: In most car accident cases, California law allows two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If your crash involved a government-owned road or vehicle, such as a city street defect, the deadline to file a claim can be as short as six months. It's best to get guidance early so you don't lose your right to recover.

items.question: What if the crash happened during Friday rush hour on I-80 or San Pablo Avenue?
items.answer: Crashes during Albany's busier travel windows, like Friday afternoons on I-80, Solano Avenue, or San Pablo Avenue, often involve multiple vehicles and conflicting accounts. We can help gather traffic camera footage, police reports, and witness information before it becomes harder to obtain. Acting quickly helps preserve the evidence that supports your claim.

items.question: Do you charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. We offer free consultations, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost to find out if you have a viable claim.
